items.title: Anthropic警告：小型AI模型数月内或实现自我复制，能推理、难关停
items.description: 10月13日，AI巨头Anthropic在其官网发布研究报告称，一些AI模型“可能再需几个月时间，就能具备自我复制的能力”，而且这一过程很难关闭。Anthropic的实验表明，小型AI模型可能只需再过几个月，就能具备在智能烤箱、杂牌Android电视盒子等商用物联网设备上自我复制的能力。这类自我复制程序将很难被彻底关闭，因为不存在一个可以集中关停的节点。不过，其复制速度可能较慢，数量翻倍时间要以天计。 阅读全文

items.author: 彭海星
items.content: 如果你是 ChatGPT 的高频用户，想必从今年 8 月开始，就碰上过一种神秘现象：ChatGPT 偶尔会在自动生成的会话标题最后，加上一些意义不明的外语单词，或是来自赌博、色情小广告的片段。 给中文会话起个英文标题倒是见怪不怪，但在标题里夹带小广告确实是全新版本。在国庆假期，我们用一晚上深挖背后可能的技术原理，得出了一些初步判断： 这不是 ChatGPT 在测试什么广告功能，也不存在隐私泄露风险，所以不必担心哪天标题里出现「疯狂水世界」；但坏消息是，它的根源可以一直追溯到 2024 年，并且最近焦头烂额的 OpenAI，似乎无心解决这个影响用户体验的技术问题。 1 月底，有开发者注意到，当使用 GPT-5.3 模型且上下文很长时，Codex 给出的消息或代码开始夹杂着中文博彩小广告，形式上和今天出现在标题末尾的字符别无二致。 2 月份，「传染病」开始蔓延到 API 端。有人用 GPT5.2-chat-latest 做工具调用时，模型没执行调用，反而输出了一串中文和少量泰文的赌博网站广告词，且系统提示词干净、没开联网搜索。 到 4 月，这一现象在开发者眼中已经司空见惯。有人在开发者社区 LINUX DO 发帖求助称，GPT 中转站疑似被挂马，时不时输出彩票广告，回复却纷纷恭喜他用上了正版 GPT——小广告就是纯血 GPT「在线发牌」的证据。

items.content: 这是人类数学协会在 OpenAI 发布大量数学研究成果后，专门写了一篇声明用来回应这件事，协会在声明中评论 OpenAI 做这件事是「 数学家们并没有要求进行这项工作 」，并呼吁所有数学家从现在开始都抵制 OpenAI。 华人数学家，菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩在自己的个人博客转载了这篇声明。很快就被网友转载为这份声明是由陶哲轩领衔发出，但事实是就连陶哲轩本人，都没有出现在这个人类数学协会的会员名单里。 于是有人开始深挖这个人类数学协会是什么来头，网友们指责该协会和 OpenAI 同样不负责，尤其是所谓的「 数学家们并没有要求进行这项工作 」言论，被认为「 是我最近读过的最滑稽、最荒谬的说法。 」 发布第二天，OpenAI 还撤下了 3 篇手稿：一处符号错误使一个核心论证失效，并连带影响两篇依赖它的论文；另外 14 篇被修订，13 篇更新了引用关系。 OpenAI 自身也承认并非所有论文都采用了 Lean 形式化方法，在他们公开的 GitHub 仓库 README 文档里提到「一些未形式化的结果可能存在问题。我们将努力尽快修复任何此类问题。」 所以，到底应该听谁的，是跟着数学界一起呼吁所有的数学家都不要再使用 OpenAI 了，还是和 OpenAI 一起，接受 AI 带来的变化，接受 AI 即将十分钟就能造出一个菲尔兹奖的现状。

Microsoft president Brad Smith is calling for urgent regulation of AI, and his argument is that consumer products like milk and washing machines have more oversight than the companies building artificial intelligence. On a recent BBC podcast , Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules. Smith also said the U.K., and not the U.S. or European Union, is best placed to lead on global safety rules. Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI), launched in 2023, receives access to major models from U.S. frontier labs before they are deployed and has quickly become a leader in AI safety testing. That role has been under threat in recent weeks, with U.S. president Donald Trump warning against “globalist” organizations, which he claims are interfering with American companies. Last month, he reportedly asked Anthropic and OpenAI to withhold new models from British testers, but AISI confirmed on Monday that it is able to access and test the latest models.

Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Dram was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him. There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet. “Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022. His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. The theory of voice being the next big interface has picked up strong momentum, with investors pouring billions of dollars into voice AI startups working on areas ranging from model makers to enterprise customer service providers, and from meeting note-takers to AI-powered dictation. Every week there is a new model or a tool release that claims to sound human and converse like one. However, in reality, that might not be the case. Enterprise voice AI platform PolyAI’s CTO Shawn Wen thinks that despite the release of full-duplex models — which can speak while listening to you — voice AI hasn’t had its “ChatGPT moment” yet. “We have reached the milestone of developing full-duplex models. The next challenge is to make reasoning very fast, so that the models can fetch answers quickly and the conversation feels natural,” he told me onstage at the HumanX conference last month. He also said that AI agents in customer service should not sound robotic and should give callers enough confidence that they can solve problems.

items.author: Anthony Ha

Get your pass and bring someone with you at 50% off. REGISTER NOW. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved. In a Saturday morning post on X , Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI. “We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI . As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”
